notes.title: Patch 2025.8.26.1
notes.notes:
[h1]Installation:[/h1]
[list]
[*] The game will now be compressed once again. This should help with read performance on most modern systems (SSD/nvme) if using a HDD you may see a slight degradation. Compressing the game files should lead to significantly better streaming performance on SSD/nvme drives. Currently, the game will be down from 55gb to 27gb.
[/list]
[h1]Fixes:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where Zarnax's drop table had more fluff than intended.
[*] Fixed an issue where Eldritch warlocks drop table had more fluff than intended.

[*] Fixed an issue where Raging Inferno R2 was not binding properly.
[*] Fixed an issue where Infernix's drop table had more fluff than intended.
[*] Fixed an issue where background NPC's could randomly change apperance when loading in.
[/list]
[h1]New:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Removed the ability to enable realistic hair. We enjoy the way it looks, but the performance cost, with potential crashes related to the hair is too steep.
[*] Added the ability to enable Volumetric Fog.
[*] Adjusting how lighting works/how global illumination look based on scalability settings(low/med/high/epic). Certain areas may be brighter or darker after these changes. Please work with us if anything is off the charts too bright or too dark. This will take time to get everything adjusted.
[*] This is to help unify how the game looks/feels on lower graphics settings. This may come with a performance cost on the lower settings, but this will get rid of the "glowy" look and feel when global illumination is low/medium.
[*] Started adding lights along all main road paths. This should help light up the main areas. We'll still be leaving some areas darker at night, to fulfill the exploration.
[*] Added light posts in Kael's Perch.
[*] Added light posts in most areas around Alden (Hidden camp/Smugglers Grotto/Silverpeak Tower)
[*] Added light posts in Willowbrook Village/Marrowhold.
[*] Added light posts in Shadowveil Refuge/Moldermire.
[*] Added light posts in Leyandel Crypt/Narthwich Village/Brightwood/Ruins of Estondar.
[*] Added light posts in Deathsworn area.
[*] Added Light posts throughout main roads in snow areas.
[*] Added light posts to all main roads in first two quadrants.
[*] Updated lighting in "origins" questline area.
[*] Updated lighting in Haven.
[*] Updated Lighting in Velenspire Ravine.
[*] Updated Lighting in Lost Catacombs.
[*] Updated Lighting in Elderbark Sanctuary
[*] Updated lighting in Stonewrought Ruins.
[*] Updated whisp to work well with new lighting. It's likely not needed in most areas now, but will still be useful for dark areas that need a light source.
[*] Whisp no longer casts shadows. This will help with a lot of the issues where it would go slightly through an object and cast a very dark shadow.
[*] Updated torch to work well with new lighting. Increased the range at which it lights up areas. Removed shadows to help it light constantly, and also increased the brightness.
[*] Added additional AI logic to help prevent enemies from getting stuck in a "Jump" loop when jumping off cliffs or areas to get to the player.
[*] Enemies that shadowstep now shadowstep behind the player, and face the player.
[*] Reduced the "recovery" time for the melee animation with main hand to the sky (shadowstep, blade dance, ect). This should allow attacks much faster after casting one of these melee abilities.
[*] Melee enemies will now check to use their "ranged" attacks more frequently. Especially when chasing players down, they'll check more frequently to try and catch players.
[*] Melee enemies in addition to checking their "ranged" attacks more frequently, there will now be a random range in between them. This should help give variety, as well as keep players on their toes.
[*] Melee enemies casting "ranged" attacks will no longer be blocked by friendlies when checking if their vision is clear to cast a ranged attack.
[*] Added the ability for background NPC's to walk around (base is random points, more specific paths/tasks will be added later).
[*] Removed Nighttime/Daytime brightness setting.
[*] Added an Overall Brightness setting.
[*] Massive updates to Deathsworn/Snow area of the world. Teleports/markers/quests will fill out here in the future.
[/list]

[h1]New:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Updated all elemental melee abilities to match their physical counterparts. Melee elemental builds felt like they didn't have enough buttons to push.
[*] Increased the amount imbue weapon fire does from 35% to 50%.

[*] Added New Enemy Codex system. Some enemies are not added as of yet, we'll be updating and adding more as we go. By default Enemies are unknown, once players deal damage to them, their name will become known, and their loot drops will display, but not show any details/names of the items. Once the enemy is killed, their loot will be visible.
[*] Changed how enemy stats are set they now use a data asset, which can easily be updated/tuned. This also allows us to display enemy stats in the new codex.
[*] Abilities that drop from enemies are now tied to their difficulty. Rank 1 abilities will drop from lower tier mobs, mid tier will drop up to rank 2, and late tier will drop all ranks.
[*] Increased the chance of receiving an ability by 100% from enemies. Previously was a 10% chance, now it's 20%.
[*] Adjusted how abilities drop from enemies. Enemies have multiple "categories" that they can drop, previously each category had a separate 10% chance to proc, then a random ability would be picked from that category would be grabbed, THEN checked if it was learned. If the ability was learned it would loop back around up to 5 times to find one not learned. After the changes, only one of these categories is picked, but the learned abilities are filtered prior, guaranteeing a new ability dropping. If all abilities from that category are learned, a new category will be picked until all of that enemy's available ability categories are exhausted.  This with the increase to 20% chance should increase the rate that abilities drop significantly, but higher abilities will no longer drop from lower tier enemies.
[*] Added enemy ability drops to codex. We decided to show these abilities after just encountering an enemy. We wanted to give players more info on fighting certain enemies to possibly farm abilities. This also helps us show how many are actually out there and available just from a secondary drop from enemies.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 2025.3.18.1
notes.notes:
[h2]Melee Updates:[/h2]
[i]We've made a pretty large adjustment to melee combat. We've had plenty of feedback saying something feels off with combat. We think this is it. In earlier versions of the game, we had stagger animations on most hits. We're going back to this. We've mirrored a lot of games that have a similar system called poise, but put our own spin on it. Below are the changes:[/i]

Reduced the reset timer on Stun Bar from 10 seconds to 5 seconds. This means stun bars will reset 50% faster.
All weapons now have a class of "Stagger" animations.
    -Daggers can cause small/medium stagger animations
    -1H Swords can cause small/medium stagger animations
    -1H Axes can cause small/medium stagger animations
    -1H Maces can cause Medium/Large stagger animations
    -2H Swords can cause Medium/Large stagger animations
    -2H Axes can cause Medium/Large stagger animations
    -2H Maces will always do Large stagger animations
    -Bows can cause Large stagger animations when dealing headshots
    -Shields will always do Large stagger animations

In order to do larger/more pronounced stagger animations, dealing damage with sneak, backstabs, and heavy attacks will increase the amount of stagger caused; increasing the stagger animation within the weapons available animations.

Players do not take stagger (animation) when getting hit. Players will take a stagger (animation) when their stun bar is full. This will help reduce the frustration of being stunned for 5 seconds, but also allowing interruption in player attacks.

Added a new stat calculation called "Toughness". This is calculated based off the amount of armor players have. By default 50% armor will have 10 stagger HP. This means a light dagger attack will need to hit you 10 times before the player receives a stagger animation. A character with 30% armor, will have their stagger HP reduced to 6. A player character with 80% armor will have their stagger HP increased to 16. This is calculated in chunks of 5% above/below the 50% mark. A players toughness (max stagger HP) will be displayed in the character stat sheet.

Enemies will always receive a stagger animation when taking damage UNLESS, their designated as boss or special mob.

Enemies that are boss or special mobs, will be stunned when their stun bar is filled only.

Enemies have "Hyper" armor while attacking. This means they cannot be staggered while in an attack animation. They can however be stunned if their stun bar fills.

notes.title: Price Adjustment and Supporter DLC!

Hello everyone,

Exciting news! We've adjusted the pricing for Heroic Kingdom as part of our commitment to gathering valuable feedback and expanding our incredible community. Since entering Early Access, we've carefully reviewed data on refunds, purchase history, and pricing to make thoughtful adjustments aimed at enhancing overall purchase satisfaction for everyone. This change isn’t about devaluing our game but rather maximizing the opportunity to collect meaningful feedback and continue improving.

We understand that pricing is an important factor when it comes to indie games. Based on industry trends and community feedback, we've noticed that players often seek great value in games that reflect creative storytelling, unique mechanics, and dedicated development efforts. By aligning our pricing with these expectations, we aim to make Heroic Kingdom accessible to more players while staying true to the quality and passion we've poured into the game.

As a token of gratitude, [u]anyone who purchased the game before the price change has been granted the Supporter DLC.[/u] [b]This DLC will keep growing, with additional content planned as our way of saying thank you for your early support.[/b]

We are thrilled to have you on this journey—your thoughts and feedback mean the world to us!

- The LilSky Team

notes.title: Patch 2025.2.20.1
notes.notes:
[h1]Fixes:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where crit increase buffs were not updating MH/OH/Ranged crit chance on character sheet.
[*] Reworked how talent % stat increases are being calculated and stored on the character. Previously, this was being calculated and directly added into the stat. For instance, if a player had 1000 strength, and 25% increased strength from talents, the 250 increase was directly stored as 1250 strength. This was causing challenges if lets say saving character with a buff, the calculation needed to remove the 250 before saving the proper 1000 strength, then re-add the 250 after the save. Obviously this is overly complicated and opens the door for many challenges (ie stat buffs not dropping correctly and infinitely increasing that stat).
[*] We've changed this entire process, to be very straightforward. If a character has 1000 strength, and 25% increase from talents, when retrieving the character's strength, the value returned is ((1000*.25) + 1000). The strength is not physically stored on the character, thus removing the potential for the extra stats to get added. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the equipped increase stats value was not updating correctly for rings/neck when loading back into game.
[*] Fixed an issue where locked items could be disenchanted.
[*] Fixed an issue where melee abilities were not benefiting from crit damage if the ability crit.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 2025.2.19.1
notes.notes:
[h1]Fixes:[/h1]

[*] Fixed an issue where dropped quest items were not adding into loot bags.
[/list]
[h1]New:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Increased the overall brightness at nighttime. If skies are clear, it should be a lot easier to see. If rain/cloudy, will still be darker.
[*] Upcoming Tertiary changes on gear (does not include Mythical/Uniques, as these are not random loot). Most of these changes are due to the upcoming addition of enchanting, which will allow players to reroll tertiaries on non mythical/unique gear.
[*] All tertiary percents will be a random value in a range. Resists will be 1-10%, Damage Increase will be 1-20%, Status Increase will be 1-5%.
[*] We'll be removing the small 2% damage increase on blues and it will be an additional resist. With the new ranges, we don't want to make it harder to get the stat you want.
[*] A legendary will now have two resists ranging from 1-10%, a Damage increase ranging from 1-20%, and status increase ranging from 1-5%. The old would be 10% static resist, 2% static damage increase, 8% static damage increase, and 5% static status increase.
[*] With these changes players should be able to get more resistances, more damage increases, while also adding more control with the use of the enchanting table to reroll for those god tier rolls.
[/list]

[h1]Enchanting(Work in progress-Expect Changes):[/h1]
[list]
[*] All Tertiaries: Players will be able to reroll all tertiaries for a moderate material cost. This is because all tertiaries will be rerolled and there is less control.
[*] Resistances: Players will be able to specifically reroll ONLY resistances on an item. This will have an increased material cost as it's more granular, with less risk of losing tertiaries players want to keep.
[*] Damage Increase: Players will be able to specifically reroll ONLY Damage increases on an item. This will have an increased material cost, with a much rarer drop item that only comes from bosses, as it's more granular, with less risk of losing tertiaries players want to keep.
[*] Status Increase: Players will be able to specifically reroll ONLY Status increases on an item. This will have an increased material cost, with a much rarer drop item that only comes from bosses, as it's more granular, with less risk of losing tertiaries players want to keep.
[*] Weapons - Players will be able to re-roll damage types with an increased material cost, requiring the rare drop from bosses.
[*] Added 4 new enchanting materials. Arcane Essence, Eternal Shard, Radiant Crystal, Runed Cores.
[*] Arcane Essence comes from disenchanting items.
[*] Eternal Shards and Radiant Crystals have a chance to drop from any mob.
[*] Runed Cores have a chance to drop from bosses only.
[/list]

[h1]Fixes:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where sneak attack was being calculated after barrier absorbs, not before.

[*] Fixed an issue where some mining nodes were not spawning correctly in the tutorial.
[/list]

[h1]Taking Damage Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] While looking into adjusting damage numbers to help readability, we found a challenge in the way incoming damage was being calculated. A very long story short, incoming damage was being calculated correctly, but because of the complexities added to the game, more and more damage was coming in much faster and more frequently. This was causing a scenario, where the incoming damage information could actually be overwritten by the next incoming damage. This is because the damage information was stored in the component globally. This was causing some inaccuracies with DoT damage, crits, and some other items.

[*] It doesn't appear this situation happened very often, but it was happening enough we needed to fix it. We intern changed how the damage is processed and there are no global values being used. This change allowed us to send much more detailed information from each attack, including MH/OH/Staff element information, while also not allowing information to be overwritten. 

[*] Because of these changes, we are making a change that we wanted to do initially, with weapons and abilities. Essentially, the way damage was processed before didn't allow us to easily just apply your MH/OH elemental effect based on the damage the ability had done, the damage needed to happen directly to apply any elemental effects. This is why you'd see multiple hits when using an ability. With this change, say you have a 2H fire sword and you use Shockwave, Shockwave hits for a 5,000 physical damage BUT also puts up a burn equal to the 2H fire sword's burn rate. This means the burn will be based on the ability damage, not an ADDITIONAL hit doing the 2H weapon damage again directly (which would also be massively less burn than basing on the ability damage).

[*] This solves two challenges. No longer is damage potentially going to be overwritten, but abilities/spells will now apply weapon elemental damage based on the ability/spell damage while reducing the amount of numbers showing on screen.

[*] Due to this change, we're also going to be making a couple of tuning adjustments, as this will undoubtably increase damage across the board.

[*] Spell forged arsenal will now only apply to spells that deal singular damage and are channeled. Bolts/Meteor/drain life/twister/ect will still apply debuffs based on the spell, but place and forget AOE type abilities will not (blizzard/firepit/acid rain/ect). This will buff channel spells significantly, as they weren't used as much as we wanted because of cast times and mobility.
[/list]

[*] Reduced the damage from corruption from 200% damage to 50% damage. This was just simply way too strong with the recent updates to void/holy tree.
[*] Added a "Queue" system for displaying DoT damage. This is to help reduce the massive amount of DoTs ticking visually. Now Holy Burns, Bleeds, and Fire Burns, and Fel Burns will display the total amount of DoT damage dealt over the previous second. This means, if there are 10 burns for example, the total tick damage will be displayed as one number (all added together) instead of 10 separate numbers.
[*] With the Queued DoT changes, we'll be increasing the size of DoT numbers when they're displayed. This will make them more readable.
[*] Added popup for opening/closing doors.

[*] Quest markers in the world map now have their name instead of the tracked number.
[*] Some quest markers with specific individual objectives (excluding killing different "types" of enemies) can now be separated. These markers will show the objective below the quest name in the world map and now will disappear when the objective is completed. This is to help alleviate what part of a quest is still active, not just two markers in world.

[h2]Crafting Station **This is the first implementation, details are likely to change**[/h2]
	1. Players will start with a set of default Bar/Leather/Armor/Weapon patterns(more with unique looks will be added).
	2. Bar patterns are found by mining the type of ore.
	3. Armor/Weapon/Jewelry patterns have a chance to "discover" a higher rank of the pattern.
		a. These higher ranks will cost more materials, but will craft at minimum the same rarity of the patter. For example, having a rank 3 heavy armor pattern(blue rarity) will ALWAYS craft a blue item.
	4. There are 3 categories of armor that can be crafted, Heavy, Medium, Light.
		a. Heavy will always have "heavy" type class rolls, for example: Tanker, Champion, or Paladin.
		b. Medium will always have "Medium" type class rolls, for example: Rogue, Shaman, or Ranger.
		c. Light will always have "Light" type class rolls, for example: Pyro, Electro, or Occultist.

	2. Scrap metal - Salvaging no longer gives materials directly, it will give scrap metal/Leather scraps/cloth based on the type and rarity.
		a. Can be used to refine into tin/copper/iron/onyx/titanium/meteorite.
		b. These refining patterns are obtained by using a lesser version. For example, refining Metal Scrap into tin/copper has a chance to give pattern to refine Metal scrap into Iron, so on and so forth.
	3. Leather scraps - obtained by salvaging gear.
		a. Leather scraps can be turned into medium/heavy leathers.
	4. Linen - obtained by salvaging gear.
  		a. Linen can be turned into cloth of any rarity - if patterns are learned.

	1. Potion patterns will no longer drop from mobs directly. They'll be available from vendors for bad luck protection, and will be "found" when gathering herbs.
	2. The same with crafting, higher tier patterns will be obtained by crafting it's lower tier variant.

[u][b]Reworked Locations:[/b][/u] Some of the original locations in the game did not meet our expectations and have been completely overhauled to give a fresh new look and feel.

We hope you enjoy these new features and enhancements. As always, your feedback is invaluable, and we can't wait to hear what you think!

notes.title: Major Reworks and Enhanced Tutorial!
notes.notes:
We are thrilled to announce a significant update to our game, bringing you a more immersive and engaging experience! 

[h2][b]This update includes:[/b][/h2]

[u][b]Revamped Camera Style:[/b][/u] Enjoy a fresh perspective with our newly reworked camera system, designed to enhance your gameplay experience.

We’ve changed how the default camera functions. Previously, the camera would not control the rotation of the player character, and the character would turn towards the direction the player was running. In this release, the player camera will rotate the character (very similar to when target-locked on an enemy). This allows the player to move in all directions while still looking forward, making blocking and parrying much easier right from the start.

[b]PLEASE NOTE: You can enable the LEGACY camera movement in the General tab of settings.[/b]

[u][b]Improved Player Animations:[/b][/u] Experience smoother and more realistic movements with our updated player animations. Each attack style now feels more unique, adding depth and variety to combat. Additionally, we’ve introduced new jog, sprint, jump, and landing animations to make all movement feel more fluid and lifelike.

[u][b]Guided Path in Tutorial:[/b][/u] New players can now benefit from a guided path in the tutorial, ensuring they do not get lost while learning the basics of the game. While we have considered implementing this feature into the main world, we are currently holding off to maintain the essence of exploration that our players love.


[b]Update your game now and explore these exciting new features![/b]

notes.title: Introducing the Basics: Upcoming Tutorial
notes.notes:
In the upcoming tutorial for Heroic Kingdom: Origins, our goal is to introduce players to the core aspects of the game. 

This tutorial will serve as a dual purpose stepping stone, aiding players through the intricate world of Heroic Kingdom by providing essential knowledge and skills, while also establishing a meaningful link between your character's past and future.

Through interactive lessons and hands-on practice, players will learn the ins and outs of combat controls, selecting and equipping the right gear that aligns with their preferred play style, how to gather valuable materials that are essential for crafting and upgrading their equipment and discovering hidden items and secrets that can aid them on their journey.

By providing a tutorial experience, we hope to ease you into the world of Heroic Kingdom and offer you the best chances to embark on a fulfilling and rewarding adventure.
